CONTENT CARD for H-SOM:
The body's trauma reactions may persist after objective danger is over, even when the person knows consciously that they are safe. With complex/developmental trauma, directly working on the deepest memory can overwhelm someone; gentle gradual work around the edges may suffice. Attribution: Buddhist nun Pema Chodron uses the phrase 'feather touch' for gentle approach; Peter Levine, founder of Somatic Experiencing, calls gentle edge-work 'pendulation'. There is a parallel in inner-child therapy: knowing what the younger part needs is not enough when one is so absorbed in the child-state that adult perspective is insufficient to offer it.

CONTENT CARD for H-CHICKEN:
The writer is encountering a chicken-and-egg dilemma. A person may be so far inside their child-state they cannot become the needed adult. Providing love is easier if one can already access at least one of their adult roles. Without that, the person might try speaking loving words while the inherited critic, numbness, panic, or urge to escape dominates the process. The uncertainty is situational, not evidence that the person is insincere.
